Scope of the role

  • Writes the compound profiles for US laboratories: a summary of what peer-reviewed studies have reported for each peptide, where that evidence stops, and bracketed citations that resolve to PubMed or the source document.
  • Covers certificate checking from the bench side — what an HPLC result can and cannot establish, why purity and fill quantity are separate measurements, and how to confirm a report with the laboratory that issued it instead of trusting a screenshot.
  • Follows FDA material that touches research peptides, including the 2026 compounding advisory committee review, and ties each regulatory statement to the document it comes from.

This profile covers what the role involves. A personal background will appear here only once it has been provided and can be stood behind.

Rules the byline follows

  • Literature claims are numbered against a References list, and each entry leads to PubMed or the original document.
  • Lot figures come from the published lab-results library, so an article and the certificate it cites show the same numbers.
  • An FDA position is quoted with the document it comes from, since agency positions change.
  • Published findings are kept apart from open questions. Laboratory research use only: nothing on dosing or administration.
